source.crossref_title: Ultralight Metallic Microlattices
source.quote: The resulting metallic microlattices exhibit densities ρ ≥ 0.9 milligram per cubic centimeter, complete recovery after compression exceeding 50% strain, and energy absorption similar to elastomers. Young's modulus E scales with density as E ~ ρ^2, in contrast to the E ~ ρ^3 scaling observed for ultralight aerogels and carbon nanotube foams with stochastic architecture.

records.notes: Density is the stated lower bound of the family (rho >= 0.9 mg/cm3), i.e. the lightest tested. A web-search snippet of a US patent family (HRL, 'Ultra-light micro-lattices') mentions 29 Pa strength at 1 mg/cc, but that page was not opened, so it is not recorded as a value. For measured values near this density see the Maloney 2013 and Zheng 2016 figure-read records below (about 1 kg/m3).

source.citation: Zheng, X.; Smith, W.; Jackson, J.; Moran, B.; Rodriguez, N.; Ye, J.; McCrea, J.; Weisgraber, T.; Spadaccini, C. Multi-scale metallic metamaterials. LLNL-JRNL-677190, 15 Sept 2015 (accepted-manuscript text of: Zheng, X.; Smith, W.; Jackson, J.; Moran, B.; Cui, H.; Chen, D.; Ye, J.; Fang, N.; Rodriguez, N.; Weisgraber, T.; Spadaccini, C. M. Multiscale metallic metamaterials. Nature Materials 15(10), 1100-1106 (2016)). The published version was not opened; wording and figure numbering of the published paper may differ from this manuscript.
source.crossref_title: Multiscale metallic metamaterials
source.location: main text, p. 9 of the manuscript
source.quote: This far exceeds first order octet metamaterials, which have a scaling power over 2.5 observed in Ni-P microlattices at relative density below 0.2% [43].

gaps: Schaedler et al. Science 2011 full text and supplement: not obtained (science.org 403, CaltechAUTHORS file access restricted, ResearchGate 403, no open-access copy per Unpaywall). Only the abstract was read, so there is no first-hand modulus or strength value for the 0.9 mg/cm3 sample. The patent snippet '29 Pa at 1 mg/cc' and the 529 kPa / 10 kPa at 0.010 g/cm3 pair (via Zhang 2019) are secondary and unverified against the paper.
Torrents et al. Acta Mater. 60 (2012) 3511-3523 (DOI 10.1016/j.actamat.2012.03.007, verified in Crossref): not accessible (ScienceDirect 403, no OA copy); abstract not read. No values recorded.

Valdevit et al. J. Mater. Res. 28 (2013) 2461-2473 (DOI 10.1557/jmr.2013.160, verified in Crossref): publisher page only; the abstract text was read only through a WebFetch summary (paraphrase, relative-density range of '0.01-10%' reported by the tool, not read verbatim); no strength values or exponents obtained. This is the source of Zheng 2016's 'over 2.5' exponent.

Salari-Sharif & Valdevit, Experimental Mechanics 54 (2014) 1491-1495 (DOI 10.1007/s11340-014-9917-8, verified in Crossref): Springer returned a client challenge; no abstract or values obtained. This is the likeliest source of a measured modulus at very low density, and of any shear modulus.

Zheng et al. Science 344 (2014) 1373-1377 (DOI 10.1126/science.1252291, verified in Crossref): NOT obtained. Its open MIT DSpace author manuscript (handle 1721.1/88084) answered HTTP 429 with Retry-After 900 s on every attempt, including a retry after 16 minutes, so no value, exponent or table was read; only the Crossref title and a search summary naming the 0.87-468 kg/m3 range were seen. No Zheng 2014 value is recorded.

Shear modulus G_c: no value measured or quoted by any source I could open, for any metallic lattice below 20 kg/m3. The Gibson-Ashby G about 3/8 E relation was not found in the Ashby 2006 text and was not obtained from the Gibson & Ashby book (not opened).

Deshpande, Ashby & Fleck, Acta Mater. 49 (2001) 1035-1040 (DOI 10.1016/S1359-6454(00)00379-7, verified in Crossref): paywalled, not opened; its prefactors are NOT recorded. The stretch/bending scalings recorded above are from Ashby 2006 (open copy) which cites it. Deshpande, Fleck & Ashby, JMPS 49 (2001) 1747-1769 (octet truss, DOI 10.1016/S0022-5096(01)00010-2, verified) also not opened.
Gibson & Ashby, Cellular Solids (book): not opened; relations taken from Ashby 2006 and from Maloney 2013 Eq. (1)-(2) which cite it.
Hollow octet nickel lattices in PMC 9738681 (Materials 2022, relative density 0.7-5%, i.e. well above 20 kg/m3 for Ni): seen only as a search hit, not opened, out of the density scope.
Per-sample tables of E, strength and density for the hollow microlattices: none printed in the papers I could read; all low-density values above are figure reads (+/-30-50%).
Gold and copper microlattices: Cu points near 4.8 mg/cm3 exist in Maloney Fig. 2/3(k) but two copper points overlap at that density and I did not record them; only the single gold point was recorded.
